l4_steps.name: Ingest threat intelligence feeds
l4_steps.system: SITA Cybersecurity Services / ISAC Aviation AISAC feed
l4_steps.input: Aviation ISAC threat bulletins, CISA alerts, commercial CTI feeds
l4_steps.output: Normalised IOC set (IPs, domains, hashes) loaded into SIEM
l4_steps.kpi: Feed ingestion latency ≤15 min from publication; IOC coverage ≥95% of subscribed feeds
l4_steps.pain_point: Aviation ISAC feed cadence is irregular; manual triage required when SITA portal and Microsoft Sentinel connector versions diverge after platform updates

l4_steps.name: Monitor SIEM for security anomalies
l4_steps.input: Log streams from Amadeus Altéa PSS, AWS Security Hub, Palo Alto NGFW, endpoint telemetry
l4_steps.output: Security alerts queue; anomaly tickets auto-created in ServiceNow Security Operations
l4_steps.kpi: Mean time to detect (MTTD) ≤4 hrs for high-severity events; alert queue SLA acknowledgement ≤15 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus Altéa PSS syslog format requires custom parser; parser breaks on Altéa quarterly patch releases causing 2–6 hr blind-spot windows

l4_steps.name: Correlate IOCs and assess threat credibility
l4_steps.system: Microsoft Sentinel / Palo Alto Cortex XSOAR
l4_steps.input: Raw SIEM alerts, enriched IOCs from threat intel feeds
l4_steps.output: Threat credibility score; escalation decision to vulnerability management or incident triage
l4_steps.kpi: False positive rate ≤12% on high-severity alerts; IOC correlation throughput ≥500 indicators/hr
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS connection endpoints (Sabre, Travelport, Amadeus GDS) generate high IOC overlap with legitimate partner traffic, inflating false-positive rates

l4_steps.name: Schedule and execute authenticated vulnerability scan
l4_steps.input: Asset inventory from AWS Security Hub and ServiceNow CMDB; approved scan windows
l4_steps.output: Vulnerability report with CVSS scores, affected asset list, and CVE references
l4_steps.kpi: Scan coverage ≥98% of in-scope assets per cycle; scan cycle ≤7 days for internet-facing assets
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew management AWS-hosted system requires coordinated scan windows with Crew Ops to avoid disrupting real-time crew tracking; missed windows extend exposure

l4_steps.name: Prioritise vulnerabilities by CVSS and asset criticality
l4_steps.input: Raw vulnerability report, asset criticality tiers from CMDB
l4_steps.output: Risk-ranked remediation backlog with SLA targets (P1–P4) in ServiceNow
l4_steps.kpi: P1 (CVSS ≥9.0) remediation SLA ≤24 hrs; P2 (CVSS 7.0–8.9) ≤7 days; mean vulnerability age ≤30 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen FliteDeck EFB tablets are classified airline OT; patches require Boeing approval and airline maintenance sign-off, extending P2 remediation to 45+ days

l4_steps.name: Execute patch deployment or emergency remediation
l4_steps.system: ServiceNow Security Operations / AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager
l4_steps.input: Approved remediation backlog item, change request from ServiceNow CAB
l4_steps.output: Patched asset record, vulnerability closure confirmation in Tenable.io
l4_steps.kpi: Patch success rate ≥99% without service disruption; emergency patch deployment ≤4 hrs for P1
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus Altéa PSS patching requires Amadeus vendor coordination and PSS freeze window; unilateral patching risks PSS instability affecting booking and check-in functions

l4_steps.name: Classify and triage incoming security alert
l4_steps.input: Alert from Microsoft Sentinel or CrowdStrike Falcon EDR
l4_steps.output: Initial triage record with classification (malware, phishing, insider, DDoS, etc.) and severity P1–P4
l4_steps.kpi: Triage completion ≤15 min for P1/P2; analyst throughput ≥20 alerts/hr per Tier-1 analyst
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC API Gateway traffic is high-volume JSON; DDoS patterns targeting NDC endpoints are difficult to distinguish from legitimate agency booking bursts without airline-specific baselines

l4_steps.name: Validate alert as true or false positive
l4_steps.input: Triage record, endpoint telemetry, network flow logs from Palo Alto NGFW
l4_steps.output: Confirmed true/false positive determination; false positives closed with tuning note
l4_steps.kpi: True positive confirmation rate ≥88%; false positive closure with tuning update ≤2 hrs
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA ACARS messages traversing legacy ground-to-air links generate unusual encoding patterns that trigger EDR heuristics; suppression rules require SITA vendor input to avoid masking real threats

l4_steps.name: Assign incident owner and escalate to IR team
l4_steps.input: Confirmed true positive with severity, initial classification
l4_steps.output: Incident ticket assigned to IR owner; P1 bridge call initiated; CISO notified for P1
l4_steps.kpi: P1 escalation to IR team ≤30 min from true positive confirmation; IR lead acknowledgement ≤15 min
l4_steps.pain_point: On-call rotation gaps during irregular flight operations (e.g., irregular operations recovery periods) delay P1 escalation when SOC team is simultaneously supporting NOC cyber requests

l4_steps.name: Activate incident response playbook
l4_steps.input: Incident ticket, threat classification, affected asset list
l4_steps.output: Active XSOAR playbook run with assigned task steps; war room opened in collaboration tool
l4_steps.kpi: Playbook activation ≤5 min of IR lead assignment; playbook coverage ≥95% of known threat categories
l4_steps.pain_point: Airline-specific playbooks for PSS compromise and GDS channel manipulation are not included in XSOAR out-of-box content library; custom playbooks require quarterly review to stay current with Amadeus Altéa version changes

l4_steps.name: Isolate affected endpoints and network segments
l4_steps.input: Confirmed affected asset list from XSOAR playbook
l4_steps.output: Isolated hosts (network contain via CrowdStrike); VLAN quarantine applied via Palo Alto policy push
l4_steps.kpi: Containment time ≤1 hr for P1; mean time to contain (MTTC) ≤2 hrs across all incidents
l4_steps.pain_point: AWS-hosted crew management system cannot be hard-isolated without triggering crew tracking outage; partial isolation (egress block only) leaves lateral movement risk

l4_steps.name: Assess OT or avionics system involvement
l4_steps.system: ServiceNow Security Operations / Tenable OT Security
l4_steps.input: Affected asset CMDB records, network topology map, CrowdStrike telemetry
l4_steps.output: OT/avionics scope determination; regulatory notification trigger decision
l4_steps.kpi: OT scope assessment completion ≤30 min of containment; 100% of OT-involved incidents flagged for TSA notification within required window
l4_steps.pain_point: EFB (Jeppesen FliteDeck) tablets on aircraft are in a grey zone between IT and OT asset classification; incident scope determination requires coordination between IT Security, Flight Operations, and Boeing technical representatives

l4_steps.name: Notify TSA and CISA per cybersecurity directive SD-04C
l4_steps.system: TSA Cybersecurity Reporting Portal / ServiceNow GRC
l4_steps.input: OT/avionics involvement confirmation, incident severity, timeline of events
l4_steps.output: TSA notification submitted within 24 hrs; CISA report filed; log preserved in ServiceNow GRC
l4_steps.kpi: TSA notification compliance: 100% on-time within 24-hr regulatory window; zero overdue reports
l4_steps.pain_point: TSA SD-04C reporting thresholds are ambiguous for incidents affecting systems that touch both IT and airline-operated networks (e.g., airport check-in kiosks on shared infrastructure); legal review adds time

l4_steps.name: Eradicate threat and preserve digital evidence
l4_steps.input: Isolated systems, threat actor TTPs, XSOAR playbook eradication task
l4_steps.output: Cleaned endpoints, forensic image stored in AWS S3 evidence bucket with chain of custody
l4_steps.kpi: Evidence collection completeness ≥99% of affected hosts; eradication verified by CrowdStrike scan before re-entry to network
l4_steps.pain_point: Volatile memory forensics on Amadeus Altéa reservation servers requires PSS vendor coordination; uncoordinated memory acquisition risks PSS process interruption affecting live bookings

l4_steps.name: Restore systems from clean validated backup
l4_steps.input: Eradication sign-off, approved recovery runbook, last known-good backup snapshot
l4_steps.output: Restored system instance, recovery validation test results, change record closed in ServiceNow
l4_steps.kpi: RTO ≤4 hrs for P1 critical systems (PSS, crew system); RPO ≤1 hr for tier-1 systems
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus Altéa PSS restoration must be sequenced with Amadeus Altéa operations team in Madrid; time zone dependency and vendor SLA of 4-hr response means RTO targets are at risk for overnight incidents

l4_steps.name: Conduct post-incident review and root cause analysis
l4_steps.input: Incident timeline, XSOAR playbook run log, forensic evidence summary
l4_steps.output: Post-incident review (PIR) report with RCA, timeline, and ≥3 action items in ServiceNow
l4_steps.kpi: PIR completion ≤5 business days for P1; 100% of action items assigned with due date; action item closure rate ≥85% within 30 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Airline operational disruption pressure (irregular operations recovery) competes with PIR scheduling; PIR action items for systemic GDS security gaps are deprioritised against commercial recovery objectives

l4_steps.name: Update controls, playbooks, and threat detection rules
l4_steps.system: Microsoft Sentinel / Palo Alto Cortex XSOAR / Tenable.io
l4_steps.input: PIR action items, new threat actor TTPs identified during incident
l4_steps.output: Updated Sentinel detection rules, revised XSOAR playbooks, new Tenable scan policies; changes logged in ServiceNow GRC
l4_steps.kpi: Detection rule update deployment ≤48 hrs of PIR sign-off; XSOAR playbook coverage improvement measured per PIR cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: Sentinel custom rules for Amadeus Altéa and Sabre GDS log formats must be regression-tested against production log samples after every rule update; lack of a dedicated security staging environment increases change risk
